issues.issue: Whether the Respondent's res judicata and issue estoppel arguments bar the Minister's stay motion
issues.applicant_position: Motion should be heard: the January 25 release order is the only one in effect and the Chief Justice did not decide mootness.
issues.respondent_position: Mootness was finally decided at the pre-hearing conference and in the earlier judicial review, so res judicata and issue estoppel apply.
issues.result_quote: As a result, I reject the Respondent’s res judicata argument.

issues.issue: Whether the stay motion is moot because the Chief Justice upheld the November 19 release order
issues.applicant_position: Each later release order supersedes the earlier one, so the dismissed review is no barrier to this motion.
issues.respondent_position: The upheld November release order is operative and the stay sought is moot.
issues.result_quote: Consequently, I find the motion and the relief sought therein to be moot.

issues.issue: Whether applying the cited case law would be an abuse of process given the Respondent's liberty interests
issues.applicant_position: Cited jurisprudence applies; the Minister's position is consistent with Federal Court and Federal Court of Appeal authority.
issues.respondent_position: Minister's position would prolong detention indefinitely through serial judicial reviews, an abuse of process.
issues.result_quote: application of the cited jurisprudence would be contrary to the interests of justice and result in an abuse of process.
